organisation: Glasgow City Youth Health Service (NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde)
CHECKED_hours: Phone line Monday – Friday, from 8.30am – 4.00pm. Clinics operate Monday-Thursday evenings, 6.30pm until 9.00pm, at health centres throughout Glasgow City.
CHECKED_eligibility_area: Young people aged 12-19 years who live in Glasgow City local authority or are registered with a Glasgow GP
in_scope: true – NHS youth health service with mental health support (short-term support for stress, anxiety and low mood, Lifelink counsellors, group sessions); not a youth club.
name: Glasgow City Youth Health Service
description: Confidential health support for young people aged 12–19 in Glasgow, including short-term help with stress, anxiety and low mood. You can refer yourself.
notes: Not an emergency service. Phone to make a referral – for young people aged 12–19 who live in Glasgow City or have a Glasgow GP.
notes_detail: Young people can refer themselves, or be referred by a teacher, school nurse, parent, GP or other organisation – the referral must be discussed with the young person first. Evening clinics run at health centres across Glasgow City. Parents, carers and young people can also use the call-back form on the contact page.
flags: Line is a referral/appointment line, not a helpline – not for crisis.
Overlaps with Lifelink (candidate 4): Lifelink counsellors deliver the mental health sessions within this service.

in_scope: true – family support service for children and young people with emotional needs, promoting positive mental health; not a youth club.

CHECKED_eligibility_area: Young person is aged 8-18 at the time of the referral; lives in Glasgow
in_scope: true (borderline) – one-to-one befriending by trained volunteers for young people coping with difficult circumstances, aiming to promote mental wellbeing; a support service rather than a youth club, but not a mental health or crisis service.
name: Volunteer Glasgow Young Persons Befriending Service
description: Free befriending for young people aged 8–18 in Glasgow who are dealing with difficult circumstances. You are matched with a trained volunteer for weekly activities.
notes: Not an emergency service. Office number, not a support line.
notes_detail: Anyone can make a referral, with the agreement of the young person and their family. Download the referral form from their website, or email befriending@volunteerglasgow.org or call 0141 226 3431 and they can email or post one out. There is no cost to families.
flags: Phone 0141 226 3431 is also Volunteer Glasgow's main office number (site header) – office/switchboard, not a support line.
Matching can take a while; waits due to high demand are stated on site.

CHECKED_eligibility_area: Youth counselling: "available for young people in specific schools across Scotland and through Youth Health Services in Glasgow". No age range stated for young people.
in_scope: true – one-to-one counselling for young people (stress, worry, low mood, etc.); not a youth club. Access is limited to specific schools and Glasgow Youth Health Services.
name: Lifelink Young Person One-to-One Counselling
description: One-to-one counselling for young people in some schools and through Glasgow's Youth Health Services. Help with stress, worry, low mood, confidence and more.
notes: Not an emergency service. Office number, not a support line.
notes_detail: Ask a teacher or guidance teacher whether your school has Lifelink counselling, or complete the referral form on their website (a teacher, parent/carer or professional can do it for you). If your school doesn't have it, call 0141 552 4434 and they will try to give you information about support in your area.
